habitat: Thornveld, mixed bushveld and riverine forest. When breeding it is attracted to thorn trees or reeds, often in large colonies, sometimes with Southern Masked Weaver or Village Weaver.
summary: A fairly common, localised resident. Both sexes are yellow, greener above, with pale yellow eyes. The breeding male has a black mask from the central crown to the throat, a rounded bib and a black bill. He is smaller than Southern Masked Weaver and Village Weaver. The female is more yellow at all times. The legs are blue-grey, not pinkish brown. The immature is like the female, with a whitish belly. The call is the swizzling typical of weavers, especially when nesting. The non-breeding male was not given a separate plumage. The Kemp paper name Lesser Masked Weaver and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Masked Weaver is larger, with a pointed bib, a black forehead and pinkish-brown legs. Lesser Masked Weaver has a rounded bib, a mask over the top of the head and blue-grey legs.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common, localised resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The non-breeding male was not given a separate plumage. The Kruger photograph shows the yellow, pale-eyed bird without a mask. No breeding-male photograph and no flight photograph were found. The grade A call is from Namibia and its licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Population figures and the Kemp name Lesser Masked Weaver were left unchanged.
